metadata.title: Communication-Efficient Learning of Deep Networks from Decentralized Data (McMahan et al., 2016)
metadata.framework: Federated learning via FedAvg: iterative model averaging with local SGD on decentralized non-IID data
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on arXiv:1602.05629 PDF text.

nodes.name: Federated learning setting
nodes.statement: Training data remains distributed across $K$ clients (e.g., mobile devices). Each client $k$ holds a local dataset $\mathcal{P}_k$ of $n_k$ examples. The data is non-IID: the local data distribution on each client may differ from the population distribution. A shared global model is learned without centralizing the data, by aggregating locally-computed updates.

nodes.name: Federated optimization objective
nodes.statement: Minimize $f(w) = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{n_k}{n} F_k(w)$ where $F_k(w) = \frac{1}{n_k} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{P}_k} f_i(w)$ is the local objective on client $k$, $n = \sum_k n_k$ is the total data size, and $f_i$ is the loss on example $i$.

nodes.name: FedSGD (Federated SGD)
nodes.statement: Each round: select a fraction $C$ of clients uniformly at random. Each selected client $k$ computes the gradient $g_k = \nabla F_k(w_t)$ on its full local dataset. The server aggregates: $w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta \sum_k \frac{n_k}{n} g_k$. This is equivalent to distributed SGD with one gradient step per round.

nodes.name: FedAvg (Federated Averaging)
nodes.statement: Each round: (1) Server sends current global model $w_t$ to a random fraction $C$ of clients. (2) Each selected client $k$ runs $E$ epochs of SGD locally on its data starting from $w_t$, producing $w_k^{t+1}$. (3) Server averages: $w_{t+1} = \sum_k \frac{n_k}{n} w_k^{t+1}$. When $E = 1$ and batch size = full local data, FedAvg reduces to FedSGD.

nodes.name: FedAvg algorithm
nodes.statement: Server: initialize $w_0$. For each round $t$: select $\max(C \cdot K, 1)$ clients $S_t$; send $w_t$ to each $k \in S_t$; receive updated $w_k^{t+1}$; aggregate $w_{t+1} \leftarrow \sum_{k \in S_t} \frac{n_k}{n} w_k^{t+1}$. Client $k$: receive $w_t$; set $w \leftarrow w_t$; for each local epoch and minibatch $b$: $w \leftarrow w - \eta \nabla F_k(w; b)$; return $w$ to server.

nodes.name: Communication efficiency
nodes.statement: FedAvg reduces communication rounds by a factor of $10$--$100\times$ compared to FedSGD by increasing local computation ($E$ epochs per round). Increasing $E$ and decreasing $C$ both reduce communication while maintaining model quality.

nodes.name: Robustness to non-IID data
nodes.statement: FedAvg works well even when data is highly non-IID (each client has examples from only 1-2 classes). While convergence can be slower with non-IID data, FedAvg still significantly outperforms FedSGD in communication efficiency.

nodes.name: Connection to local SGD / parallel SGD
nodes.statement: FedAvg is algorithmically equivalent to local SGD (Zinkevich et al., 2010) with periodic averaging. The key novelty is the application to the federated setting with non-IID data, unbalanced data sizes, and unreliable communication, plus the empirical demonstration that many local steps work well even with non-IID data.
